question: Should OpenClaw core add a first-party per-agent backup/restore/clone contract, and what should it include or exclude for credentials, transcripts, workspaces, and SQLite state?
rationale: The requested workflow crosses destructive local state writes, credential/session portability, archive trust, and overlap with broader backup/snapshot work, so automation cannot safely choose the product and security boundary.

options.title: Design Minimal Core Per-Agent Restore
options.body: Define a preview-first core `--agent`/`--as` lifecycle with safe extraction, path rewrites, credential policy, transcript policy, rollback, and focused tests before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Backup Umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue open as a requirement under the broader native backup/restore design so archive format and restore semantics are decided once.

options.title: Route Most Scope To Plugins
options.body: Limit core to missing APIs or docs if maintainers decide per-agent cloning should be provided by a ClawHub plugin or external workflow.

recommendation.title: Design Minimal Core Per-Agent Restore
recommendation.body: Define a preview-first core `--agent`/`--as` lifecycle with safe extraction, path rewrites, credential policy, transcript policy, rollback, and focused tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice is primarily a core product/security boundary decision spanning backup, restore, sessions, and plugin scope, and this person has recent routing context in the area.
